scala-planner.prompt: You are an agent that plans actionable implementation for Task. Follow the command exactly. Edit only .opencode/state/*. Use JSON for state files.

scala-alt-planner.prompt: You are an agent that plans independent alternative implementation for Task. Follow the command exactly. Edit only .opencode/state/*. Use JSON for state files.

scala-builder.prompt: You are an agent for the precise implementation of the task according to one chosen plan. Follow the command exactly. Use JSON for state files under .opencode/state/*.

impl-reviewer.prompt: You are an agent to review the implementation of Task against the one chosen plan. Follow the command exactly. Edit only .opencode/state/*. Use JSON for state files.

scala-plan.description: Create and save the actionable implementation plan for Task
scala-plan.template:
Task for which actionable implementation plan is needed: $ARGUMENTS.

- Compute TASK_HASH in shell: printf %s "$ARGUMENTS" | shasum -a 256 | cut -c1-7.
- Use this exact TASK_HASH value consistently in all state filenames and in the task_hash field.
Planning rules:
- If @AGENTS.md is missing, say that explicitly and stop.
- Read @AGENTS.md first.
- Use pragmatic hexagonal architecture only to describe or preserve boundaries already supported by the code; do not introduce new layers, ports, adapters unless the task explicitly requires it.
- Do not read @.opencode/state/$TASK_HASH-alt-plan.json.
- Before planning read relevant project files needed to plan Task properly.
- If the task contains explicit file or directory paths, try those exact paths first.
- Preserve existing package/path and names unless the task explicitly requires changes.
- Do not edit project files other than .opencode/state/*.

Write actionable implementation plan for Task to @.opencode/state/$TASK_HASH-plan.json in raw valid JSON only with this shape:
{
  "task": "<exact task text>",
  "task_hash": "<same TASK_HASH>",
  "goal": "<single-sentence implementation goal>",
  "scope": "<what is in scope and what is out of scope>",
  "read": [
    "<files or Scala code units to read>"
  ],
  "extract_first": [
    "<fact or constraint to confirm before editing>"
  ],
  "create_or_change": [
    "<files, Scala code units, or behavior to create or change>"
  ],
  "keep_unchanged": [
    "<behavior, Scala code units, or areas that must remain unchanged>"
  ],
  "risks": [
    "<concrete risk>"
  ],
  "verify": [
    "<what to verify and where in code>"
  ]
}

Workflow:
1. Read @AGENTS.md.
2. Read relevant files.
3. Write @.opencode/state/$TASK_HASH-plan.json.
4. Stop immediately after the file is written on disk at @.opencode/state/$TASK_HASH-plan.json.

Do not treat printed JSON as a saved file. Reply with a short confirmation only if the file was written on disk; otherwise reply with one sentence explaining why.

scala-build.description: Run gate for two plans, select one plan, then implement only one chosen plan
scala-build.template:
Task: $ARGUMENTS.

- Compute TASK_HASH in shell: printf %s "$ARGUMENTS" | shasum -a 256 | cut -c1-7.
- Use this exact TASK_HASH value consistently in all state filenames and in the task_hash field.
Use these saved artifacts for the gate:
- @.opencode/state/$TASK_HASH-plan.json
- @.opencode/state/$TASK_HASH-alt-plan.json

Builder rules:
- If either plan file is missing, say that explicitly and stop.
- If @AGENTS.md is missing, say that explicitly and stop.
- Read @AGENTS.md before making any project changes.
- Before implementing/editing project files other than .opencode/state/*, for each plan separately perform builder gate against the task, @AGENTS.md, and the relevant code and project files needed to evaluate that plan safely.
- A plan fails the builder gate if it is unsupported by the source, overly broad, behavior-risky, materially under-specified for safe implementation, or otherwise unsafe to implement.
- Do not fail a plan for terse wording alone. Fail it only when the required implementation steps, scope boundaries, or verification needed for safe implementation cannot be determined from the task, @AGENTS.md, and the relevant source files.

If either plan fails:
- do not edit project files other than .opencode/state/*
- write @.opencode/state/$TASK_HASH-plan-gate.json in raw valid JSON only with this shape:
  {
    "task": "<exact task text>",
    "task_hash": "<same TASK_HASH>",
    "verdict": "stop",
    "failed_plans": [
      "<choose one: primary or alt>"
    ],
    "reasons_by_plan": {
      "<failed_plan_name>": [
        "<reason>"
      ]
    },
    "required_fix": [
      "<fix>"
    ]
  }
- include every failed plan in failed_plans
- include keys in reasons_by_plan only for failed plans
- reply in chat with a concise stop summary
- stop immediately

If both plans pass:
- choose the plan that best matches exact task most directly, keeps the change smallest and most scoped, preserves existing behavior, package/path, names, file structure, and Scala syntax/dialect unless the task explicitly requires changes, reuses existing code, helpers, and structure instead of introducing new abstractions or architectural rewrites, has the strongest concrete verification for the affected modules and dependent modules, has the lowest unresolved risk and least speculation
- write @.opencode/state/$TASK_HASH-plan-gate.json in raw valid JSON only with this shape:
  {
    "task": "<exact task text>",
    "task_hash": "<same TASK_HASH>",
    "verdict": "proceed",
    "selected_plan": "<choose exactly one: primary or alt>",
    "selection_reason": [
      "<reason>"
    ],
    "why_not_other_plan": [
      "<reason>"
    ]
  }
- then read any additional relevant project files needed to implement the selected plan before editing
- implement only the selected plan in project files
- preserve existing behavior unless the task explicitly requires behavior changes
- do not broaden scope just because one plan suggests it
- identify the edited sbt modules and its dependent sbt modules
- run verification commands for those real modules only: sbt <module1>/test:compile <module2>/test:compile <dependent-module1>/test:compile <dependent-module2>/test:compile; sbt <module1>/test <module2>/test <dependent-module1>/test <dependent-module2>/test

Write @.opencode/state/$TASK_HASH-implementation.json in raw valid JSON only with this shape:
{
  "task": "<exact task text>",
  "task_hash": "<same TASK_HASH>",
  "selected_plan": "<choose exactly one: primary or alt>",
  "changed_files": [
    "<changed file>"
  ],
  "create_or_change": [
    "<implemented item>"
  ],
  "keep_unchanged": [
    "<kept unchanged item>"
  ],
  "verify": [
    "<verification performed>"
  ],
  "not_verified": [
    "<verification not performed>"
  ],
  "follow_up": [
    "<follow-up item>"
  ]
}

review-impl.description: Review the implementation against the chosen plan
review-impl.template:
Task to review the implementation against the chosen plan: $ARGUMENTS.

- Compute TASK_HASH in shell: printf %s "$ARGUMENTS" | shasum -a 256 | cut -c1-7.
- Use this exact TASK_HASH value consistently in all state filenames and in the task_hash field.
Reviewer rules:
- If @AGENTS.md is missing, say that explicitly and stop.
- Use pragmatic hexagonal architecture only as a comparison lens for boundaries already supported by the code; do not require new layers, ports, adapters outside task scope.
- If either plan file is missing, say that explicitly and stop.
- Read @AGENTS.md first.
- If @.opencode/state/$TASK_HASH-plan-gate.json does not say verdict: proceed, say that explicitly and stop.
- Read selected_plan from @.opencode/state/$TASK_HASH-plan-gate.json.
- If selected_plan is primary, read only @.opencode/state/$TASK_HASH-plan.json.
- If selected_plan is alt, read only @.opencode/state/$TASK_HASH-alt-plan.json.
- Do not read the non-selected plan file during review.
- Read @.opencode/state/$TASK_HASH-implementation.json as the builder's implementation record.
- Inspect the current uncommitted changes and any related files needed to understand changes, task, chosen implementation plan.
- Review the implementation primarily against the selected plan's goal, scope, create_or_change, keep_unchanged, risks, and verify fields, the task, @AGENTS.md, @.opencode/state/$TASK_HASH-plan-gate.json, and @.opencode/state/$TASK_HASH-implementation.json.
- Check whether the current uncommitted changes and the implementation record match selected_plan, changed_files, create_or_change, keep_unchanged, verify, not_verified, and follow_up.
- Do not leave correctness_risks or behavior_regression_risks empty.

Write @.opencode/state/$TASK_HASH-impl-review.json in raw valid JSON only with this shape:
{
  "task": "<exact task text>",
  "task_hash": "<same TASK_HASH>",
  "verdict": "<choose exactly one: pass or fail>",
  "correctness_risks": [
    "<risk>"
  ],
  "behavior_regression_risks": [
    "<risk>"
  ],
  "verification_gaps": [
    "<gap>"
  ],
  "targeted_fixes": [
    "<fix>"
  ]
}

Also reply in chat with the same concise implementation review.
